title: Maria Callas's birth chart
metaDescription: Maria Callas's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.5° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a conjunction: Mars and Saturn within 0.7°, drive wired to structure. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 9.5° Sagittarius — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Sagittarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 18.7° Sagittarius, Mars holds 29.1° Libra — in the old shorthand, a mind that decides at speaking speed; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Saturn — a conjunction holding at 0.7°. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all. Behind it, Venus sextile Mars at 1.4°, and Mercury trine Neptune at 1.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mercury in Sagittarius at 18.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Libra at 29.1° is in detriment; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 1.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Libra at 28.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: fire 4, air 2, water 2 across the elements, and mutable 4, cardinal 3, fixed 1 across the modalities. Venus crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day, so its sign is left open. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.9° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
